records.title: Commons Journal vol. 214, 11 and 25 Nov 1958: City of Cardiff (Leckwith Common) Compulsory Purchase Order 1957 laid, and no petition reported
aliases: Journals of the House of Commons 1958-59, Leckwith Common order
records.place_text: Leckwith Common, parish of Leckwith (City of Cardiff order)
records.description: Two entries in the printed Journals of the House of Commons, volume 214 (session 1958-59), on the City of Cardiff (Leckwith Common) Compulsory Purchase Order, 1957, which came before Parliament under the Statutory Orders (Special Procedure) Act 1945. On Tuesday 11 November 1958 the Minister of Housing and Local Government (Henry Brooke) laid a copy of the order, dated 8 September 1958, with his certificate under section 2 of the Act (p.22). On Tuesday 25 November 1958 the Chairman of Ways and Means laid the report of the Chairmen of both Houses under section 3 that no petition had been presented against it, listed with the Appleton Common Compulsory Purchase Order 1958 (p.40). The volume index repeats both entries (pp.328 and 346). The volume contains no other entry for Leckwith and does not mention Llandough or Cogan.
records.transcript:
11 November 1958, p.22 (margin: Acquisition of Land): "Mr. Brooke presented, pursuant to the directions of an Act of Parliament,—Copy of an Order, dated 8th September 1958, entitled the City of Cardiff (Leckwith Common) Compulsory Purchase Order, 1957, with a Certificate by the Minister of Housing and Local Government under Section 2 of the Statutory Orders (Special Procedure) Act, 1945. Ordered, That the said Paper do lie upon the Table."

25 November 1958, p.40 (margin: Statutory Orders (Special Procedure)): "The Chairman of Ways and Means presented, pursuant to the directions of an Act of Parliament,—Report by the Chairman of Committees of the House of Lords and the Chairman of Ways and Means in the House of Commons under Section 3 of the Statutory Orders (Special Procedure) Act, 1945, That no Petition has been presented against— (1) the City of Cardiff (Leckwith Common) Compulsory Purchase Order, 1957, and (2) the Appleton Common Compulsory Purchase Order, 1958. Ordered, That the said Paper do lie upon the Table."

Index, p.328, ACQUISITION OF LAND: "Orders (Act): 1957:—City of Cardiff (Leckwith Common) Compulsory Purchase, 22". Index, p.346, STATUTORY ORDERS (SPECIAL PROCEDURE): "That no Petitions have been presented against the following Orders: 1957:—City of Cardiff (Leckwith Common) Compulsory Purchase, 40".
records.transcript_status: Read on 3 November 2026 from the text layer of the scanned volume, with the interleaved columns separated by hand, and checked against the page images of pp.22 and 40.
records.interpretation: With hindsight and wider context: the order was made by Cardiff Corporation in 1957 and confirmed by the Minister of Housing and Local Government on 8 September 1958; the London Gazette of 31 October 1958 (p.6652) gives that confirmation under section 5 of the Physical Training and Recreation Act 1937, which points to land for recreation. Because the land was common land, the confirmed order went through special parliamentary procedure: it was laid before both Houses with the Minister's certificate (11 November 1958), a short period followed in which a petition could be deposited, and on 25 November 1958 the Chairmen of the two Houses reported that none had been. No joint committee hearing followed. What it shows: the two parliamentary steps of the order, their dates, and that the petition route in Parliament was not used. What it does not show: the land taken, its area or boundaries, the owners, occupiers or holders of rights, any compensation, the map, or any objection made at the earlier local inquiry. It names no parish other than Leckwith and no person other than the Minister and the Chairman of Ways and Means. What cuts against a simple reading: no petition does not mean no objection. Objections to a compulsory purchase order were heard at the local inquiry before confirmation, and press reports of a 1958 Leckwith Common inquiry are catalogued separately; a petition to Parliament was a further formal step with a short deadline. Equally, nothing on these pages records a dispute over title to the common. The plotting of the order land against neighbouring parcels is not checked; the certified map is held by the Parliamentary Archives and has not been read.

records.title: Ordnance Survey Book of Reference to the 1:2500 plan of the parish of Llandough juxta Cardiff (bound volume dated 1877)

date.precision: year of the bound volume; survey date of the parish not read

records.place_text: Parish of Llandough juxta Cardiff (Llandough-juxta-Penarth), Hundred of Dinas Powis; the same volume covers Leckwith
records.description: The Ordnance Survey's printed book of reference (area book) for the first 1:2500 survey of the parish. It lists every numbered parcel on the plan, nos 1 to 166 with 99a, 111a, 142a and 146a, and a detached part, giving each parcel's area in acres and its land use (pasture, arable, wood, houses and gardens, roads). Railway parcels (126, 151), part of the dock (152), two reservoir parcels (23, 122), the church and graveyard and the school and playground are among them. An index to places gives the map sheets for named places, all on 6-inch sheet XLVII: Baptist Chapel, Cardiff Water Works Penarth Reservoir, Cogan-pill, Elm Cottage, Greenway Cottage, Highlands, Lime Works, Llandough juxta Cardiff, Llandough Farm, Llandough House, Oak Cottage, Pen-y-lan, Post Office, Rectory, School, Station, St Dochdwy's Church and Ty-mawr. The same volume holds the book of reference for Leckwith.

records.interpretation: With hindsight and wider context: area books were published by the Ordnance Survey to accompany the first 1:2500 county series plans and record only the parcel number, area and use. What it shows: the parcel numbering and areas of the whole parish as surveyed in the 1870s, the presence of railway, dock and reservoir land by then, and the map sheets for named places. This numbering is the key that later deposited plans and the 1910 valuation used, so it is the bridge between the c.1841 tithe apportionment and later records. What it does not show: owners, lessees or occupiers of any parcel, or any transfer or acquisition. What cuts against reading more into it: a reservoir or railway parcel in the 1870s shows the land was then in that use, not how or from whom it was acquired; which tithe fields each OS parcel matches is not checked.

records.title: London Gazette, 25 Nov 1859: Cardiff Waterworks Company Bill, the Cogan Pill Reservoir and an intended Llandough Reservoir
records.place_text: Parish of Llandough (Llandough-juxta-Penarth): Cogan Pill Farm; a field near the road from Leckwith to Dinas Powis, about 600 yards west of Llandough Church; mains through Llandough, Cogan and Leckwith
records.description: Parliamentary notice of the Cardiff Waterworks Company for the 1860 session (construction of new works, purchase of land, extension of district, further money, amendment of the Cardiff Waterworks Act 1853). In Llandough it describes a reservoir lately constructed by the Company at Cogan Pill Farm (called the Cogan Pill Reservoir), an aqueduct from it to an intended reservoir called the Llandough Reservoir, to be made in a field in the occupation of Thomas Rees near the road from Leckwith to Dinas Powis and about 600 yards west of Llandough Church, an aqueduct from the Cogan Pill Reservoir through Llandough, Cogan and Penarth towards Penarth Church, and powers to purchase lands by compulsion and by agreement. The Bill became the Cardiff Waterworks Act 1860.
records.transcript: "To construct and maintain an aqueduct or aqueducts commencing at a certain reservoir lately constructed by the Company at Cogan Pill Farm, in the parish of Llandough, hereinafter called the Cogan Pill Reservoir, and terminating in a certain reservoir hereinafter described, intended to be constructed near the road leading from Leckwith to Dinas Powis, and hereinafter called the Llandough Reservoir, all in the parish of Llandough, in the county of Glamorgan. To construct and maintain a reservoir (in this notice called the Llandough Reservoir), with works and conveniences connected therewith, in a field in the occupation of Thomas Rees, near the said road leading from Leckwith to Dinas Powis, and about 600 yards westward of Llandough Church, all in the parish of Llandough, in the county of Glamorgan." […] "To purchase by compulsion and by agreement, lands, tenements, houses, messuages, springs, streams, mills, waters, and hereditaments, or to take leases of the same" […]
records.transcript_status: Read on 3 November 2026 from the OCR text of the Gazette PDF (pp.4375-4376), with the two interleaved columns separated by hand; […] marks text left out; not checked against the page image.
records.interpretation: With hindsight and wider context: a waterworks Bill of this kind was accompanied by deposited plans and a book of reference naming the owners, lessees and occupiers of each plot. The Bill became the Cardiff Waterworks Act 1860 (23 & 24 Vict. c.141); whether the Llandough Reservoir was authorised and built as noticed is not checked here. The Ordnance Survey book of reference for the parish (1877 volume, AR-OS-BOOKREF-1877-LLANDOUGH) lists two reservoir parcels and indexes the Cardiff Water Works Penarth Reservoir, so at least one reservoir existed by the 1870s. What it shows: statutory waterworks in Llandough from the 1850s, earlier than the railway Bills of 1876-1897, and the one occupier the notice names in the parish. What it does not show: owners, the plots, any price or compensation, or which tithe field the intended reservoir field was. What cuts against a wider reading: the only Llandough occupier named is Thomas Rees, so the notice does not tie this work to any other occupier's land.

records.place_text: Parish of Llandough (Llandough-juxta-Penarth), about five chains south-west of the Merry Harrier Inn, where the Dinas Powis-Cogan Pill road meets the Cogan-Llandough road
records.description: Parliamentary notice for the 1859 session to incorporate a company to supply water to shipping using Penarth harbour and docks and to the parishes of Penarth, Cogan, Llandough, Leckwith and Llandaff. It proposes reservoirs in St Andrews (on Dinas Powis Brook), in Llandough (south-west of and about five chains from the Merry Harrier Inn) and in Penarth (west of Penarth Church), with connecting mains through Llandough, Cogan, Leckwith and Llandaff. Owners and occupiers are not named in the notice.

records.title: London Gazette, 21 Nov 1856: Ely Tidal Harbour and Railway Bill, a railway from near a house in Llandough to the River Ely
aliases: Penarth Harbour, Dock and Railway Bill 1857
records.place_text: Parish of Llandough (Llandough-juxta-Penarth): from a point near a house in the parish, to the south-west bank of the River Ely between Cogan Pill and Cwtch-y-Cwn
records.description: Parliamentary notice for the 1857 session by the Ely Tidal Harbour and Railway Company (incorporated by an Act of 21 July 1856, 19 & 20 Vict. c.200; renamed the Penarth Harbour, Dock and Railway Company by the Act of 1857, 20 & 21 Vict. c.78). Among the works it lists a railway from a point near a house in Llandough, then in the occupation of John Stuart Corbett, to the south-west bank of the River Ely between Cogan Pill and Cwtch-y-Cwn, in the parishes of Llandough and Penarth. Plans and a book of reference were to be deposited. The company's earlier notice (London Gazette, 20 November 1855, issue 21816 p.4329) lists its works in Llandaff, Llandough, Leckwith, Cogan, St Mary Cardiff, Penarth Flats or West Mud, and Penarth.
records.transcript: "Also a railway from and out of the said intended railway, at a point near to a house in the parish of Llandough, in the occupation of Mr. John Stuart Corbett, to a point on the south-west bank of the River Ely, midway or thereabouts between Cogan Pill and Cwtch-y-Cwn, which said railway will be situate in the parish of Llandough and Penarth, or one of them" […]
records.transcript_status: Read on 5 November 2026 from the OCR text of the Gazette PDF; […] marks text left out; not checked against the page image.
records.interpretation: With hindsight and wider context: the deposited plans with books of reference and lists of owners, lessees and occupiers are catalogued by the Parliamentary Archives as HL/PO/PB/3/plan1856/E4 and HL/PO/PB/3/plan1857/E2. The company's land papers at The National Archives include RAIL 1057/1503 (1858-1866), a draft conveyance of lands in the parishes of Llandough and Penarth from Baroness Windsor and others, and RAIL 1057/1504/1, an agreement of 30 April 1856 as to the conveyance of lands. What it shows: statutory railway and dock works over land in Llandough from 1855-57, earlier than the waterworks notices of 1858-59. What it does not show: which plots were taken, or who owned them. Which John Stuart Corbett is meant is not checked. What cuts against a wider reading: a notice of intended works is not evidence that every work was made or that any particular plot changed hands.

records.title: London Gazette, 22 Nov 1895: London and South Wales Railway Bill, Railways No.1 and No.5 in Llandough-juxta-Cardiff
records.place_text: Parish of Llandough-juxta-Cardiff: junction with the Barry Railway east of the Cogan Tunnel; the Penarth Moors by the Llandough sidings of the Taff Vale Railway Penarth branch
records.description: Parliamentary notice for the 1896 session to incorporate the London and South Wales Railway Company, with a main line from the Barry Railway near Cardiff to Kingswood in Gloucestershire and on towards London. Railway No.1 was to begin in the parish of Llandough-juxta-Cardiff by a junction with the Barry Railway; Railway No.5 was to lie wholly in that parish, from Railway No.1 on the Penarth Moors to a junction with the Penarth branch of the Taff Vale Railway. The notice seeks powers for the compulsory purchase of lands and states that plans and a book of reference were to be deposited.
records.transcript: "Railway No. 1.—A railway commencing in the parish of Llandough-juxta-Cardiff, in the county of Glamorgan, by a junction with the Barry Railway at a point 48 yards, or thereabouts (measured in an easterly direction along such railway), from the eastern face of the Cogan Tunnel thereon […]" "Railway No. 5.—A railway wholly situate in the said parish of Llandough-juxta-Cardiff, commencing by a junction with the intended Railway No. 1 at a point on the Penarth Moors 220 yards, or thereabouts, measured in an easterly direction from the bridge under the Penarth Branch of the Taff Vale Railway Company at the northern end of the Llandough sidings upon such branch, and terminating by a junction with the said branch […]"
records.transcript_status: Read on 6 November 2026 from the OCR text of the Gazette PDF, with the interleaved columns separated by hand; […] marks text left out; not checked against the page image.
records.interpretation: With hindsight and wider context: the deposited plans and book of reference are catalogued by the Parliamentary Archives as HL/PO/PB/3/plan1896/L13 (with /L13/2: book of reference and list of owners, lessees and occupiers) and by Glamorgan Archives as Q/D/P/607 (plan and reference book, sealed). The National Archives holds heads of agreement between the promoters and the Great Western Railway, January 1896 (RAIL 252/1132). What it shows: an intended compulsory purchase of land in Llandough-juxta-Cardiff for a trunk line in the 1896 session. What it does not show: which plots, or who owned or occupied them. What cuts against a wider reading: whether the Bill was passed is not checked; a scheme that was not authorised took no land.

records.place_text: Parishes of Llandough-juxta-Cardiff (urban district of Penarth), Leckwith and Canton: from the Penarth branch east of the Cogan Tunnel to the Penarth Curve of the Great Western Railway
records.description: Parliamentary notice of the Barry Railway Company for the 1898 session. Railway No.1 was to begin in Llandough-juxta-Cardiff by a junction with the company's Penarth branch east of the Cogan Tunnel and end in Canton by a junction with the Penarth Curve of the Great Western Railway, passing through Llandough-juxta-Cardiff, Canton and Leckwith. The notice also lists a road in Llandough-juxta-Cardiff and Cogan, seeks powers to purchase lands compulsorily or by agreement, and states that plans of the lands with a book of reference naming owners or reputed owners, lessees or reputed lessees and occupiers were to be deposited with the Clerk of the Peace for Glamorgan by 30 November 1897.
records.transcript: "A Railway (No. 1) commencing in the parish of Llandough-juxta-Cardiff, in the urban district of Penarth, and county of Glamorgan, by a junction with the Penarth branch railway of the Company at a point 9 chains or thereabouts, measured along that railway eastward from the eastern face of the Cogan Tunnel, and terminating in the parish of Canton and county borough of Cardiff by a junction with the Penarth Curve railway of the Great Western Railway Company […] which said proposed railway will be made in the said parishes of Llandough-juxta-Cardiff […] Canton […] and in the parish of Leckwith, in the rural district of Llandaff and Dinas Powis […]"
